punchline: For women whose chronic PTSD hadn't responded to other treatments, a weekly yoga class brought significantly more relief than the comparison group got.
thirty_sec: Bessel van der Kolk argues that understanding why you feel threatened doesn't stop your body reacting as if you are. So his Trauma Center tried trauma-sensitive yoga with women whose chronic PTSD hadn't improved with other treatment. The classes focused on breathing and noticing body sensations without being overwhelmed. Compared with a control group, the yoga group's symptoms dropped significantly more. The body, it seems, has to practise feeling safe.
question: Have you ever found that a physical activity calmed you more than talking something through?
